name: What if my house is older and may not meet current code for an in-law suite?

mainEntity.name: What if my house is older and may not meet current code for an in-law suite?
mainEntity.text: What if my house is older and may not meet current code for an in-law suite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older homes can still be good candidates for an in-law suite, but they often reveal issues that affect budget and schedule. Common problems include undersized electrical panels, outdated plumbing, weak framing, poor insulation, and missing fire protection. Those items may need to be upgraded before the new space can pass inspection. The key is to inspect the house early so the design reflects the real conditions, not just the assumed ones. If the home has several deficiencies, the project may cost more than expected, but it can still be worthwhile if the new suite solves a real family need. A thorough preconstruction review is the best way to avoid surprises after demolition starts.
acceptedAnswer.description: Older homes often need upgrades before an in-law suite can be approved, especially for electrical, plumbing, structural, and fire separation requirements. The project may still be possible, but the existing house should be evaluated early. Hidden deficiencies are one of the biggest reasons budgets change during construction.
